item.title: Gambit 1.3.2
item.description:
# Gambit 1.3.2
Released November 22, 2026.
## On 1.3.0 or 1.3.1? Download the DMG by hand, once
**If you are running 1.3.0 or 1.3.1, this build will not arrive through the update button. Download it yourself, once:**
**https://github.com/Frenzyz/gambit-releases/releases/latest/download/Gambit.dmg**
Open the DMG and drag Gambit to Applications, replacing the copy you have. From 1.3.2 onward, updates install themselves again — this is the only time you have to do it by hand.
This is worth a paragraph of explanation, because the reason is the whole story of the release.
Gambit's updater is a small helper app that lives inside Gambit, called `Autoupdate`. Its job is to quit Gambit, put the new copy in place, and open it again. Since 1.3.0, that helper has been built in a way macOS refuses to run. macOS looks at its signature, sees it claiming permissions that only Gambit itself is allowed to hold, and kills it the moment it starts — before it can do anything, and without saying why.
So every time you pressed Update, the download arrived, the signature checked out, and then the thing that installs it was silently killed. Gambit showed you *"An error occurred while running the updater. Please try again later."* Pressed again, it failed again. There was nothing wrong with your network, your disk, or the build it was trying to fetch.
**The trap is that an update cannot repair the updater that delivers it.** The only way to replace a helper that cannot run is to not use it — which means putting this one in place by hand, once. After that, `Autoupdate` works, and updates arrive normally again.
The build is fixed on our side: the helper is now signed on its own, without the permissions that got it killed, and the build refuses to produce a release if a helper ever carries them again. That last part matters — this shipped twice, and both times it was invisible until someone tried to update.
## Everything else in this release
Nothing else changed for you. This is 1.3.1 with a working updater.
If you are coming from 1.3.0, you also get 1.3.1's fixes — your Mac serves the remote screen again after a relaunch, a turn started from the phone can act without the Mac's Control chip, and a long address stays inside its pill on the iPhone.
---
Your passkeys still do not work: this build's provisioning profile is missing the Web Browser entitlement, so WebAuthn is unavailable. It is unchanged from 1.3.0 and is being fixed separately.
